title: Introduce credit-based admission and decompose batch control plane
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: The continuous batching controller and the slot allocation/scheduler logic have accrued coupling and ad-hoc heuristics over multiple optimizations. This makes it hard to reason about tail latency, to implement graceful degraded modes when the KV cache is saturated, and to test admission policies independently. We also have tech debt in the admission path: it relies on global counters and coarse hotkey heuristics that break under bursty workloads.

Goal: Decompose the batch control plane into two cooperating components: (1) a lightweight credit-based admission controller (credit-adm) that enforces per-session and per-model credits with backpressure signals, and (2) a simplified batch coordinator responsible only for grouping admitted requests into lanes and assigning slot leases. The credit-adm will own slow-path safeguards (circuit-breaker semantics) that can trigger fallback to lighter model variants or queueing. This ticket includes dependency upgrades required for the refactor, API compatibility shims, and a targeted perf cleanup of the KV cache hotpath to reduce latency under overload.

Out of scope: full rewrite of prefetch subsystem, model-variant selector logic (only hook points), or UI surface changes in Console (observability integration covered in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Introduce credit-adm library with unit tests covering credit grants, spend, and expiration
Batch coordinator split completed; continuous-batcher core logic moved behind new coordinator interface
KV cache hotpath optimizations merged that reduce median KV lookup CPU by >=12% on synthetic hotkey replay
End-to-end e2e benchmark: under 10k RPS mixed traffic, 99th percentile latency for text-generate path does not regress more than 5% compared to baseline
Graceful circuit-breaker path triggers for simulated KV saturation and routes 100% of overflow to configured fallback model variant
testing_plan: Unit tests for credit accounting, expiration, and concurrency (race-scenarios)
Integration test harness: inject synthetic burst with hotkey frequency; assert credits throttle instead of dropping requests
Load test scenario in staging with real models (small/gptq) at 50%, 100%, 150% of target RPS to observe fallback behavior
Chaos test: kill a slot-allocator instance during batch commit and ensure coordinator heals without losing in-flight credits
Canary rollout: 5% of traffic in dedicated canary pool for 48h, escalate on latency or error SLO violations
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch behind feature-flag: runtime.credit_adm.v1
Deploy library and coordinator shim to staging, run full e2e suite
Enable feature-flag for canary pool (5% traffic) and run 48h soak
If stable, increase to 25% for 24h, then 100% on a rolling deploy across zones
Post-rollout: enable Console telemetry dashboard panels for credit utilization and breaker activations
risks: Regression in latency if coordinator batching heuristics incorrectly size lanes
Incorrect credit expiry could cause request starvation for long-running sessions
Fallback model routing may increase unit cost during sustained overload
Dependency upgrades may introduce subtle async runtime behavior changes (see related_links PRs)
implementation_notes: Credit-adm will be implemented as an independent crate/module with a small public interface: allocate_credit(session_id, model_id, amount), spend(session_id, amount), snapshot(session_id)
Coordinator interface: accept(admitted_request) -> lane_assignment; batch commit unchanged except for lease handshake simplification
KV hotpath: inline a fast-path that detects local shard hits and avoids metric histogram allocation; avoid global locks for short-lived lookups
Compatibility shim: legacy admission APIs will be supported for 2 releases; add telemetry to measure shim usage
Follow-up tickets will expose per-customer quota mapping and chargeback metrics
